summary: Paper W3161169265 presents a thermal goodness evaluation (TGV) methodology for 3D-IC floorplans using GSRC benchmarks (n100, n200, n300) on 64×64, 128×128, and 256×256 grids. The scenario describes a four-layer TSV-based 3D IC with steady-state thermal analysis at 45 nm technology, power densities randomly assigned from 10⁵–10⁷ W/m², and comparisons against HotSpot peak temperature predictions. Studio did not run. The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable because the paper evaluates a 3D heterogeneous architecture (four-layer stack with inter-layer thermal coupling via TSVs), not a 2D planar floorplan. The deterministic gate blocked execution due to missing mandatory inputs: no floorplan block list (1–128 blocks required) and no power_w object populated with module-level power assignments. The custom_2d_steady experiment kind is incompatible with this 3D multi-layer geometry and thermal model. Evidence extraction identified 41 items but all lack valid pinned asset locators, preventing independent verification. Critical missing data include quantified layer thicknesses, material thermal properties (conductivity, specific heat), exact module coordinates and power values for GSRC benchmarks, HotSpot configuration parameters beyond 'defaults', and floorplanning tool source code. The paper's thermal observable (peak temperature, K) and regime (steady-state) are defined but not independently verifiable against extracted evidence. Physical mismatches include random power density assignment without justification, absent module activity documentation, and asymmetric TSV thermal modeling (zero-power assumption conflicting with inter-layer heat transfer inclusion). Studio assumptions documented the 45 nm node, power range, four-layer topology, and 5 K temperature sensitivity threshold, but these cannot be validated without access to actual floorplan data, HotSpot logs, or reproducible configurations.
limitations: Paper scenario describes a 3D architecture (four-layer TSV-based IC), which is out of scope for 2D planar thermal screening; the not_2d_applicable verdict is deterministic and blocking
No floorplan block definitions or power_w assignments provided; Studio cannot initialize a custom_2d_steady experiment without 1–128 blocks and populated per-block power values
Evidence extraction yields 41 items but all lack pinned asset locators (asset_id, valid page anchors); independent verification of parameter claims is not possible
GSRC benchmark module coordinates, dimensions, and power density assignments not included in paper or supplementary materials; reproducibility of numerical results cannot be established
HotSpot configuration parameters documented as 'defaults' without specification; baseline thermal simulation conditions are undocumented and non-reproducible
Material thermal properties (conductivity, specific heat) and layer thicknesses (active Si, SiO₂, TIM) referenced only in Figure 1 schematic; quantitative values not extracted or validated
Floorplanning tool source code [13], [14], [15] not linked; evolutionary computation algorithm details (population size, mutation rate, convergence) are missing
Random power density assignment methodology (10⁵–10⁷ W/m² range) lacks justification; no validation against actual 45 nm technology specifications or workload characterization
TSV islands modeled as zero-power modules in TGV but included in inter-layer heat transfer (dist_z calculation); this asymmetry is not resolved in the paper
Grid discretization sensitivity limited to three fixed sizes (64×64, 128×128, 256×256); no finer grid validation or convergence analysis provided
Temperature measurement sensor placement in HotSpot and GUT selection criteria in TGV not documented; thermal observable localization is ambiguous
Correlation coefficient results (0.89 for n100, 0.96 for all benchmarks) are based on 30–60 floorplan samples; generalization to unseen 3D IC configurations is unvalidated

Success rate analysis (97% for ΔT > 5 K, 87% for ΔT < 5 K) derived from only 140 pair comparisons on three benchmarks; statistical significance and boundary behavior near 5 K threshold require larger datasets
Floorplan pair comparison methodology (10 samples, 140 comparisons) introduces selection bias; systematic coverage of design space is not demonstrated
No transient analysis performed; all evaluation is steady-state only, limiting applicability to dynamic workloads or thermal cycling scenarios
A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object
